    public static RayHit TracerRaycastMipReseedClosedForm(float3 origin, float3 dir, ChunkStore store,
        AirMipData mips, float maxDist = 128f)
    {
        RayHit result = new RayHit { hit = false, steps = 0 };
        float3 rayStart = origin * 10f;
        float3 rayDir = math.normalize(dir);
        int3 step = (int3)math.sign(rayDir);
        float3 tDelta = math.abs(1f / rayDir);
        int3 voxel = CoordMath.WorldToVoxel(origin);
        float3 tMax = new float3(
            step.x > 0 ? (voxel.x + 1f - rayStart.x) : (rayStart.x - voxel.x),
            step.y > 0 ? (voxel.y + 1f - rayStart.y) : (rayStart.y - voxel.y),
            step.z > 0 ? (voxel.z + 1f - rayStart.z) : (rayStart.z - voxel.z)
        ) * tDelta;
        float currentDist = 0f;
        float maxVoxelDist = maxDist * 10f;
        int3 lastNormal = int3.zero;

        while (currentDist < maxVoxelDist && result.steps < 1000)
        {
            result.steps++;

            byte mat = store.GetVoxel(voxel);
            if (mat != 0)
            {
                result.hit = true;
                result.voxelCoord = voxel;
                result.material = mat;
                result.normal = lastNormal;
                return result;
            }

            bool leapt = false;
            for (int k = mips.NumLevels; k >= 1; k--)
            {
                int shift = 3 + k;
                int3 cell = voxel >> shift;
                int3 dims = mips.DimsOfLevel(k);
                if (mips.Levels[k - 1][AirMip.FlatIndex(cell, dims)] == 0u)
                {
                    int spanVoxels = 8 << k;
                    int3 spanMin = cell << shift;
                    LeapSpanReseedClosedForm(ref voxel, ref tMax, ref currentDist, tDelta, step,
                             rayStart, spanMin, spanVoxels, ref lastNormal);
                    leapt = true;
                    break;
                }
            }
            if (leapt) continue;

            int3 brickCoord = CoordMath.VoxelToBrick(voxel);
            if (BrickIsUniformAir(store, brickCoord))
            {
                LeapBrickO1ReseedClosedForm(ref voxel, ref tMax, ref currentDist, tDelta, step, rayStart, brickCoord, ref lastNormal);
                continue;
            }

            StepDda(ref voxel, ref tMax, ref currentDist, tDelta, step, ref lastNormal);
        }

        return result;
    }
}

// ==========================================
// FILE: Assets/CoreEngine/Rendering/RaymarchStripped.compute

#pragma kernel CSMain

#include "../Coord/CoordMath.hlsl"
#include "../Memory/StructHeaders.hlsl"

// [DIAGNOSTIC] Register-pressure A/B sibling of Raymarch.compute. Mode 1
// (Reseed) only, Beauty output only. No debug buffer, no debug pixel, no
// traversal-mode branch, no debug-view branch, no iteration-cap uniform.
// Every kept line is copied verbatim from Raymarch.compute's mode-1 path -
// nothing here is re-derived, only omitted. If this kernel is meaningfully
// faster than the full one at identical dispatch/pose, the full kernel's
// always-compiled debug/mode branches are causing register spillage; if not,
// this hypothesis is ruled out too.

RWTexture2D<float4> ResultTexture;
StructuredBuffer<uint> ClipmapBuffer;
StructuredBuffer<uint> BrickDataBuffer;

StructuredBuffer<uint> AirMip1;
StructuredBuffer<uint> AirMip2;
StructuredBuffer<uint> AirMip3;
StructuredBuffer<uint> AirMip4;
uint4 _AirMipDims0;
uint4 _AirMipDims1;
uint4 _AirMipDims2;
uint4 _AirMipDims3;
uint  _AirMipLevelCount;

float4x4 _CameraInverseProjection;
float4x4 _CameraInverseView;
float3 _CameraPos;
uint4 _WindowDimsBricksPacked;

uint4 _WindowDimsChunksPacked;

uint ReadClipmap(int3 brickCoord, uint3 windowDimsBricks)
{
    int3 chunkCoord   = brickCoord >> 4;
    int3 wrappedChunk = chunkCoord & (int3)(_WindowDimsChunksPacked.xyz - 1);
    int  chunkSlot    = wrappedChunk.x
                      + (wrappedChunk.y * (int)_WindowDimsChunksPacked.x)
                      + (wrappedChunk.z * (int)_WindowDimsChunksPacked.x * (int)_WindowDimsChunksPacked.y);
    int3 localBrick = brickCoord & 15;
    int  local      = LocalBrickIndex(localBrick);
    return ClipmapBuffer[(chunkSlot * 4096) + local];
}

int AirMipFlatIndex(int3 cell, uint3 dims)
{
    int3 wrapped = cell & (int3)(dims - 1);
    return wrapped.x
         + wrapped.y * (int)dims.x
         + wrapped.z * (int)dims.x * (int)dims.y;
}

uint ReadAirMip(int level, int3 cell)
{
    if (level == 1) return AirMip1[AirMipFlatIndex(cell, _AirMipDims0.xyz)];
    if (level == 2) return AirMip2[AirMipFlatIndex(cell, _AirMipDims1.xyz)];
    if (level == 3) return AirMip3[AirMipFlatIndex(cell, _AirMipDims2.xyz)];
    return AirMip4[AirMipFlatIndex(cell, _AirMipDims3.xyz)];
}

float ReseedTMaxAxis(int voxelAxis, float rayStartAxis, float tDeltaAxis, int stepAxis)
{
    return (stepAxis > 0 ? (voxelAxis + 1.0 - rayStartAxis) : (rayStartAxis - voxelAxis)) * tDeltaAxis;
}

void LeapSpanReseed(inout int3 voxel, inout float3 tMax, inout float currentDist,
                     float3 tDelta, int3 step, float3 rayStart, int3 spanMin, int spanVoxels,
                     inout int3 normal)
{
    int3 exitCount = int3(
        step.x > 0 ? (spanMin.x + spanVoxels - voxel.x) : (voxel.x - (spanMin.x - 1)),
        step.y > 0 ? (spanMin.y + spanVoxels - voxel.y) : (voxel.y - (spanMin.y - 1)),
        step.z > 0 ? (spanMin.z + spanVoxels - voxel.z) : (voxel.z - (spanMin.z - 1)));

    precise float tExitX = tMax.x + (exitCount.x - 1) * tDelta.x;
    precise float tExitY = tMax.y + (exitCount.y - 1) * tDelta.y;
    precise float tExitZ = tMax.z + (exitCount.z - 1) * tDelta.z;

    int axis;
    if (tExitX <= tExitY) axis = (tExitX <= tExitZ) ? 0 : 2;
    else                  axis = (tExitY <= tExitZ) ? 1 : 2;

    float tHit = (axis == 0) ? tExitX : ((axis == 1) ? tExitY : tExitZ);

    const float eps = 1e-4;
    int nonExitGuard = spanVoxels + 1;
    int guardX = min(exitCount.x, nonExitGuard);
    int guardY = min(exitCount.y, nonExitGuard);
    int guardZ = min(exitCount.z, nonExitGuard);

    if (axis == 0)
    {
        voxel.x += step.x * exitCount.x;
        tMax.x = ReseedTMaxAxis(voxel.x, rayStart.x, tDelta.x, step.x);
    }
    if (axis == 1)
    {
        voxel.y += step.y * exitCount.y;
        tMax.y = ReseedTMaxAxis(voxel.y, rayStart.y, tDelta.y, step.y);
    }
    if (axis == 2)
    {
        voxel.z += step.z * exitCount.z;
        tMax.z = ReseedTMaxAxis(voxel.z, rayStart.z, tDelta.z, step.z);
    }

    if (axis != 0) { int g = 0; [loop] while (tMax.x <= tHit + eps && g < guardX) { voxel.x += step.x; tMax.x += tDelta.x; g++; } }
    if (axis != 1) { int g = 0; [loop] while (tMax.y <= tHit + eps && g < guardY) { voxel.y += step.y; tMax.y += tDelta.y; g++; } }
    if (axis != 2) { int g = 0; [loop] while (tMax.z <= tHit + eps && g < guardZ) { voxel.z += step.z; tMax.z += tDelta.z; g++; } }

    currentDist = tHit;
    normal = (axis == 0) ? int3(-step.x, 0, 0)
           : ((axis == 1) ? int3(0, -step.y, 0)
                          : int3(0, 0, -step.z));
}

[numthreads(8, 8, 1)]
void CSMain(uint3 id : SV_DispatchThreadID)
{
    uint3 _WindowDimsBricks = _WindowDimsBricksPacked.xyz;

    uint width, height;
    ResultTexture.GetDimensions(width, height);
    if (id.x >= width || id.y >= height) return;

    float2 uv = float2((id.x + 0.5) / width, (id.y + 0.5) / height) * 2.0 - 1.0;
    float4 target = mul(_CameraInverseProjection, float4(uv.x, uv.y, 1, 1));
    float3 rayDir = mul(_CameraInverseView, float4(normalize(target.xyz / target.w), 0)).xyz;

    rayDir.x = abs(rayDir.x) < 1e-6 ? (rayDir.x >= 0 ? 1e-6 : -1e-6) : rayDir.x;
    rayDir.y = abs(rayDir.y) < 1e-6 ? (rayDir.y >= 0 ? 1e-6 : -1e-6) : rayDir.y;
    rayDir.z = abs(rayDir.z) < 1e-6 ? (rayDir.z >= 0 ? 1e-6 : -1e-6) : rayDir.z;

    float3 rayStart = _CameraPos * 10.0;

    int3 step = int3(sign(rayDir.x), sign(rayDir.y), sign(rayDir.z));
    float3 tDelta = abs(1.0 / rayDir);

    int3 voxel = WorldToVoxel(_CameraPos);

    float3 tMax = float3(
        step.x > 0 ? (voxel.x + 1.0 - rayStart.x) : (rayStart.x - voxel.x),
        step.y > 0 ? (voxel.y + 1.0 - rayStart.y) : (rayStart.y - voxel.y),
        step.z > 0 ? (voxel.z + 1.0 - rayStart.z) : (rayStart.z - voxel.z)
    ) * tDelta;

    float currentDist = 0;
    int steps = 0;
    bool hit = false;
    uint mat = 0;
    int3 normal = 0;

    while (currentDist < 1280.0 && steps < 400)
    {
        steps++;

        bool leapt = false;
        [loop]
        for (int k = (int)_AirMipLevelCount; k >= 1; k--)
        {
            int shift = 3 + k;
            int3 cell = voxel >> shift;
            if (ReadAirMip(k, cell) == 0u)
            {
                int spanVoxels = 8 << k;
                int3 spanMin = cell << shift;
                LeapSpanReseed(voxel, tMax, currentDist, tDelta, step, rayStart, spanMin, spanVoxels, normal);
                leapt = true;
                break;
            }
        }
        if (leapt) continue;

        int3 brickCoord = VoxelToBrick(voxel);
        uint handle = ReadClipmap(brickCoord, _WindowDimsBricks);
        bool isDense = (handle & 0x80000000) != 0;

        if (isDense)
        {
            uint poolIdx = handle & 0x3FFFFFFF;
            int3 localVoxel = LocalVoxelIndex3D(voxel);
            uint vIdx = (uint)LocalVoxelIndex(localVoxel);
            uint packedData = BrickDataBuffer[(poolIdx * 128) + (vIdx >> 2)];
            uint shift = (vIdx & 3) * 8;
            mat = (packedData >> shift) & 0xFF;

            if (mat != 0) { hit = true; break; }

            if (tMax.x < tMax.y)
            {
                if (tMax.x < tMax.z) { voxel.x += step.x; currentDist = tMax.x; tMax.x += tDelta.x; normal = int3(-step.x, 0, 0); }
                else                 { voxel.z += step.z; currentDist = tMax.z; tMax.z += tDelta.z; normal = int3(0, 0, -step.z); }
            }
            else
            {
                if (tMax.y < tMax.z) { voxel.y += step.y; currentDist = tMax.y; tMax.y += tDelta.y; normal = int3(0, -step.y, 0); }
                else                 { voxel.z += step.z; currentDist = tMax.z; tMax.z += tDelta.z; normal = int3(0, 0, -step.z); }
            }
            continue;
        }

        mat = handle & 0xFF;
        if (mat != 0) { hit = true; break; }

        {
            int3 bMin = brickCoord * 8;
            LeapSpanReseed(voxel, tMax, currentDist, tDelta, step, rayStart, bMin, 8, normal);
        }
    }

    float4 color = float4(0.2, 0.4, 0.8, 1.0);
    if (hit)
    {
        float ndotl = max(0.2, dot(float3(normal), normalize(float3(0.5, 1.0, 0.2))));
        color = float4(0.5 * ndotl, 0.5 * ndotl, 0.5 * ndotl, 1.0);
        if (mat == 2) color = float4(0.6 * ndotl, 0.6 * ndotl, 0.6 * ndotl, 1.0);
    }
    ResultTexture[id.xy] = color;
}

// ==========================================
// FILE: Assets/CoreEngine/Simulation/FluidCA.compute
// ==========================================
// Assets/CoreEngine/Simulation/FluidCA.compute
//
// Phase 5b, file 1 of §13's ordered list: FluidReferenceCPU's Clear / Intent+Claim
// / Commit ported to HLSL.
//
// §13: "Port FluidReferenceCPU's logic to HLSL line-by-line, exactly as Phase 2
// ported the raymarch DDA -- with a working CPU reference already in hand, this
// is a translation exercise, not a design exercise." Every kernel below names
// the FluidReferenceCPU method it is a translation of. If you change behaviour
// here, change it there first and re-run the EditMode suite, or the oracle stops
// being an oracle (§7.2).
//
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// NO ATOMICS IN THE CLAIM PATH (§7.3, 8.4)
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The claim is an ORDINARY STORE, not InterlockedMin. §7.3: "a single aligned
// word store cannot tear on any real GPU, so the slot ends up holding exactly
// one of the candidate values, never a corrupted mix. Which one survives is
// arbitrary -- and that's fine, because §7.8 already establishes correctness
// requires only conservation and steady-state behavior, never a specific
// deterministic winner."
//
// There is exactly one InterlockedAdd in this file, in AllocSlot, and it is NOT
// in the claim path -- it is a free-list bump for slot allocation. 8.4's rule is
// specifically about the claim contention hotspot at convergence points (the
// base of a waterfall); a promotion counter has no such hotspot. Do not "tidy"
// the claim into an atomic.
//
// THE PLAIN-WRITE SAFETY CLAIM IS NOT VERIFIED ON METAL BY THIS FILE. §7.3
// says to "verify on Metal specifically in Phase 5b" with a flood test. That
// test is FluidClaimStress.compute + the Phase5b_ClaimStress scene, and it has
// to be run by a human on the target Mac. Nothing here should be read as
// evidence that the plain write is safe on this toolchain.
//
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// WHAT THIS SHADER MAY AND MAY NOT WRITE (§0.1 invariant 1, §7.2)
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// It reads terrain from the clipmap and NEVER writes it. Motion decisions leave
// this shader only as an append to OpList, which the CPU reads back and applies
// through ChunkStore.SetVoxel. The CPU remains the sole terrain writer with zero
// exception.
//
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// TWO BEHAVIOURS PORTED FROM PHASE 5a AS BEHAVIOUR, NOT AS SPEC SENTENCES
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// PHASE_5A_COMPLETION.md §5 and §9 flag these explicitly. Both are load-bearing
// for reaching rest at all; porting §7.6's literal wording instead reproduces
// the non-convergence 5a measured (5-7 lateral moves/tick still at tick 2000).
//   1. The sleep counter resets ONLY on a move that DESCENDED. A lateral move
//      ages it. See CSSweep.
//   2. Only a DESCENDING move requests a neighbourhood wake. A lateral shuffle
//      changes no fluid level, and waking from it re-promotes sleeping
//      neighbours with a fresh budget, sustaining the shuffle forever.
//      See CSCommit.

#pragma kernel CSClear
#pragma kernel CSPromote
#pragma kernel CSReact
#pragma kernel CSIntent
#pragma kernel CSCommit
#pragma kernel CSSweep
#pragma kernel CSWakeScan
#pragma kernel CSFinalize

#include "../Coord/CoordMath.hlsl"

// =========================================================================
// A.5 FluidSlot -- CPU mirror is FluidSlotGpu in FluidGpuSimulation.cs and the
// two MUST stay byte-identical. Fields are A.5's; the widths are not (A.5 packs
// ushort/byte, this uses uint) because a structured buffer wants 4-byte lanes
// and §0.1 invariant 9 says take the dumb version. 24 bytes.
// =========================================================================
struct FluidSlot
{
    int  brickDataIndex;    // home brick; next-free index when the slot is free
    uint localVoxelOffset;  // 0..511 within the home brick (C.1)
    uint materialID;        // cached; validated against the home byte (§7.3)
    uint sleepCounter;
    uint viscosityPhase;
    uint stateFlags;        // Appendix B
};

// A.9 FluidWriteOp -- the bounded command-list record (§7.2, §3.9).
// A.9 FluidWriteOp, EXTENDED to a MOVE op. 32 bytes.
//
// A.9 describes a single-cell write, "(voxelPosition, newMaterial)". That
// cannot survive an edit landing between a move being DECIDED on the GPU and
// APPLIED on the CPU: the move's two halves (write dst, clear src) are separate
// records, so validating one and dropping it while the other applies changes
// mass. Measured: place_block reported GPU 250 vs CPU 249 and mine_drop
// GPU 249 vs CPU 250 -- gain and loss of exactly one drop, both in the two
// scenarios that edit terrain while ops are in flight.
//
// So a move is ONE record naming BOTH cells, and the CPU applies both or
// neither after re-validating against current terrain. Reactions, which are
// genuinely single-cell, set OP_HAS_SRC to 0 and carry their expected previous
// material instead. This is a deliberate, documented extension of A.9.
struct FluidWriteOp
{
    int3 dst;       // gets `material`
    uint material;  // [7:0] new material, [8] WAKE, [23:16] expected material at dst
    int3 src;       // gets Air, when OP_HAS_SRC
    uint flags;
};
#define OP_WAKE_BIT    (1u << 8)
#define OP_HAS_SRC     (1u << 0)
#define OP_EXPECT_SHIFT 16

// ---- Appendix B stateFlags ----
#define FLAG_AWAKE        (1u << 0)
#define FLAG_BID_PLACED   (1u << 1)
#define FLAG_WON_CLAIM    (1u << 2)
#define FLAG_FORCE_DEMOTE (1u << 3)
#define FLAG_EVALUATED    (1u << 4)   // reserved [7:4], same use as the CPU reference
#define FLAG_DESCENDED    (1u << 5)

#define NONE (-1)
#define AIR  (0u)

// ---- Terrain, read-only (same buffers and same addressing the raymarcher uses) ----
StructuredBuffer<uint> ClipmapBuffer;
StructuredBuffer<uint> BrickDataBuffer;
uint4 _WindowDimsChunksPacked;   // .xyz = resident window size in CHUNKS (pow2)
int4  _WindowOriginBricksPacked; // .xyz = window origin in bricks
uint4 _WindowDimsBricksPacked;   // .xyz = window size in bricks

// ---- Fluid state ----
RWStructuredBuffer<FluidSlot> FluidSlots;
RWStructuredBuffer<int>       ClaimBuffer;    // cell -> winning slot, or NONE
RWStructuredBuffer<int>       SlotAtBuffer;   // cell -> owning slot, or NONE
RWStructuredBuffer<int>       ReactedBuffer;  // cell -> 1 if a reaction spoke for it
// Cells a DESCENDING commit touched this tick. CSWakeScan re-promotes their
// mobile neighbours immediately, on the GPU, in the same tick.
//
// WHY THIS IS NOT LEFT TO THE CPU'S op-driven wake: that path is latency-bound
// (§7.2's 1-3 frame readback), so a drop whose support vacated got its wake a
// round-trip late and had already slept. The CPU oracle wakes instantly, so the
// two settled into DIFFERENT valid rest states -- measured as up to 12 drops
// stranded a layer high, with mass conserved exactly. §7.6's "any adjacent edit
// re-promotes" is about the EDIT path; fluid waking its own neighbours is the
// CA's own business and belongs on the GPU where it can be immediate.
RWStructuredBuffer<int>       WakeMark;
RWStructuredBuffer<uint>      Counters;       // [0]=slotHighWater [1]=freeCursor [2]=opCount(dbg) [3]=wakeCount
// THE OP-LIST IS ONE PLAIN STRUCTURED BUFFER, READ BACK WITH ONE REQUEST.
//
// It was an AppendStructuredBuffer plus a separate counter buffer. That needed
// two AsyncGPUReadback requests per frame, and the SMALL COUNTER one failed
// intermittently with hasError and no reason logged by Unity -- while the large
// op-list request beside it always succeeded. Five narrower fixes did not move
// it (in-flight cap, ring buffering, replacing CopyCount with a shader counter,
// 4 requests -> 2, back-pressure), including a version where both requests read
// the SAME buffer and only the first still failed.
//
// So the transport changed shape instead: element 0 is a HEADER carrying the op
// count (written by CSFinalize), elements 1.. are the ops. One buffer, one
// request per frame, on the buffer type and size that was already reliable.
// OpCounters is still the allocation cursor, but it is no longer read back.
RWStructuredBuffer<FluidWriteOp> OpsBuffer;
RWStructuredBuffer<uint> OpCounters;

RWStructuredBuffer<int>       WakeRequests;   // cells the CPU asked to wake (§7.6)

// §10.4's per-subsystem diagnostic dump, GPU side. "This converts a vague
// failure into the exact state that caused it -- the single highest-leverage
// debugging aid when code is generated fast and bugs arrive fast."
// Cleared by the CPU every tick and read back small; slots are:
//   [0] wake requests seen by CSPromote      [1] slots ALLOCATED
//   [2] promote rejected: cell already owned [3] promote rejected: not mobile
//   [4] awake slots CSIntent processed       [5] claims CSIntent placed
//   [6] claims CSCommit saw                  [7] commits CSCommit applied
//   [8] intent: orphan-freed                 [9] intent: no legal destination
//  [10] commit reject: home mismatch        [11] commit reject: dst not air
RWStructuredBuffer<uint>      DebugCounters;
#define DBG(i) InterlockedAdd(DebugCounters[i], 1u)


// ---- Material registry (A.7 flags + §7.4 tick intervals), 256 entries ----
StructuredBuffer<uint>  MaterialFlags;
StructuredBuffer<uint>  MaterialTickInterval;
StructuredBuffer<uint>  ReactionSelfProduct;   // [self*256 + other], 0xFFFFFFFF = no reaction
StructuredBuffer<uint>  ReactionOtherProduct;

#define FLAG_IS_FLUID         (1u << 0)
#define FLAG_IS_FALLING_SOLID (1u << 1)
#define FLAG_IS_MOBILE_MASK   (FLAG_IS_FLUID | FLAG_IS_FALLING_SOLID)

// ---- Active region (§7.4 near-player scope). Power-of-two dims, bitwise only. ----
int4  _RegionOriginVoxels;   // .xyz
uint4 _RegionDimsVoxels;     // .xyz, each a power of two
uint4 _RegionShifts;         // .x = log2(dims.x), .y = log2(dims.y)
int4  _PlayerVoxel;
int   _ActiveRadiusVoxels;
int   _Tick;
uint  _SlotCapacity;
uint  _RegionCellCount;
uint  _WakeRequestCount;
uint  _MaxOpsPerFrame;
uint  _SleepTicks;        // EngineConfig.FLUID_SLEEP_TICKS

/// Reserve one op slot. Returns false when the frame's budget is spent, which
/// is a MOTION loss (the move simply does not happen this tick), never a mass
/// loss -- the terrain bytes are untouched and the slot retries next tick.
bool EmitOp(int3 dst, uint material, int3 src, uint flags, uint expectAtDst)
{
    uint idx;
    InterlockedAdd(OpCounters[0], 1u, idx);
    if (idx >= _MaxOpsPerFrame) return false;
    FluidWriteOp op;
    op.dst = dst;
    op.material = material | (expectAtDst << OP_EXPECT_SHIFT);
    op.src = src;
    op.flags = flags;
    OpsBuffer[1 + idx] = op;      // +1: element 0 is the header
    return true;
}
// (EmitOp lives here, AFTER the uniform block: HLSL requires declaration
//  before use and _MaxOpsPerFrame is declared just above.)

// =========================================================================
// Region addressing -- bitwise only (§0.1 invariant 2)
// =========================================================================
bool InRegion(int3 v)
{
    int3 r = v - _RegionOriginVoxels.xyz;
    return r.x >= 0 && r.y >= 0 && r.z >= 0
        && r.x < (int)_RegionDimsVoxels.x
        && r.y < (int)_RegionDimsVoxels.y
        && r.z < (int)_RegionDimsVoxels.z;
}

int RegionIndex(int3 v)
{
    int3 r = v - _RegionOriginVoxels.xyz;
    return r.x | (r.y << _RegionShifts.x) | (r.z << (_RegionShifts.x + _RegionShifts.y));
}

int3 RegionVoxel(int index)
{
    int sx = (int)_RegionShifts.x, sy = (int)_RegionShifts.y;
    int mx = (int)_RegionDimsVoxels.x - 1, my = (int)_RegionDimsVoxels.y - 1;
    int3 r = int3(index & mx, (index >> sx) & my, index >> (sx + sy));
    return r + _RegionOriginVoxels.xyz;
}

// =========================================================================
// Terrain read -- the SAME lookup Raymarch.compute uses (ReadClipmap + dense
// body unpack). Kept structurally identical on purpose: if the raymarcher and
// the CA ever disagree about what material is in a cell, the bug is here.
// =========================================================================
uint ReadClipmapHandle(int3 brickCoord)
{
    int3 chunkCoord   = brickCoord >> 4;
    int3 wrappedChunk = chunkCoord & (int3)(_WindowDimsChunksPacked.xyz - 1);
    int  chunkSlot    = wrappedChunk.x
                      + (wrappedChunk.y * (int)_WindowDimsChunksPacked.x)
                      + (wrappedChunk.z * (int)_WindowDimsChunksPacked.x * (int)_WindowDimsChunksPacked.y);
    int3 localBrick = brickCoord & 15;
    int  local      = LocalBrickIndex(localBrick);
    return ClipmapBuffer[(chunkSlot * 4096) + local];
}

/// Material at a world voxel. Returns AIR outside the resident window, which
/// matches ChunkStore.GetVoxel's documented behaviour for an unloaded chunk.
uint SampleVoxel(int3 voxel)
{
    int3 brickCoord = VoxelToBrick(voxel);
    int3 rel = brickCoord - _WindowOriginBricksPacked.xyz;
    if (rel.x < 0 || rel.y < 0 || rel.z < 0 ||
        rel.x >= (int)_WindowDimsBricksPacked.x ||
        rel.y >= (int)_WindowDimsBricksPacked.y ||
        rel.z >= (int)_WindowDimsBricksPacked.z)
        return AIR;

    uint handle = ReadClipmapHandle(brickCoord);
    if ((handle & 0x80000000u) == 0u) return handle & 0xFFu;   // uniform brick

    uint poolIdx = handle & 0x3FFFFFFFu;
    uint vIdx    = (uint)LocalVoxelIndex(LocalVoxelIndex3D(voxel));
    uint packed  = BrickDataBuffer[(poolIdx * 128) + (vIdx >> 2)];
    return (packed >> ((vIdx & 3u) * 8u)) & 0xFFu;
}

bool IsMobile(uint material)      { return (MaterialFlags[material] & FLAG_IS_MOBILE_MASK) != 0u; }
bool IsFluidMaterial(uint material){ return (MaterialFlags[material] & FLAG_IS_FLUID) != 0u; }
uint TickIntervalOf(uint material)
{
    uint t = MaterialTickInterval[material];
    return t == 0u ? 1u : t;
}

int  HomeIndexOf(FluidSlot s)  { return (s.brickDataIndex << 9) | (int)s.localVoxelOffset; }

/// The home address is stored A.5-style (brick + local offset) over the REGION's
/// own cell indexing, not the world brick pool -- the region is the CA's address
/// space, exactly as the sandbox was for the CPU reference.
void SetHome(inout FluidSlot s, int regionCellIndex)
{
    s.brickDataIndex   = regionCellIndex >> 9;
    s.localVoxelOffset = (uint)(regionCellIndex & 511);
}

bool WithinActiveRadius(int3 v)
{
    int3 d = v - _PlayerVoxel.xyz;
    return (d.x * d.x + d.y * d.y + d.z * d.z) <= (_ActiveRadiusVoxels * _ActiveRadiusVoxels);
}

// C.7 tie-variety hash. Identical constants and mixing to
// FluidReferenceCPU.Hash so the two implementations shuffle the same way; §7.8
// does not require frame-exact agreement, but a translation should not gratuitously
// differ where matching is free.
uint HashCell(int x, int y, int z, int tick, int salt)
{
    uint h = 2166136261u;
    h = (h ^ (uint)x) * 16777619u;
    h = (h ^ (uint)y) * 16777619u;
    h = (h ^ (uint)z) * 16777619u;
    h = (h ^ (uint)tick) * 16777619u;
    h = (h ^ (uint)salt) * 16777619u;
    h ^= h >> 15; h *= 2246822519u; h ^= h >> 13;
    return h;
}

/// Four lateral directions in a hash-derived order. Same three-bit scheme as
/// FluidReferenceCPU.BuildLateralOrder: each direction is tried FIRST with
/// probability exactly 1/4, which is what §13's "water drifts one direction
/// consistently -> parity/tie-break bias" failure signature is about.
void LateralOrder(int3 c, int salt, out int2 dirs[4])
{
    uint h = HashCell(c.x, c.y, c.z, _Tick, salt);
    bool zFirst = (h & 1u) != 0u;
    int px0 = (h & 2u) != 0u ? -1 : 1;
    int pz0 = (h & 4u) != 0u ? -1 : 1;
    if (zFirst)
    {
        dirs[0] = int2(0, pz0);  dirs[1] = int2(0, -pz0);
        dirs[2] = int2(px0, 0);  dirs[3] = int2(-px0, 0);
    }
    else
    {
        dirs[0] = int2(px0, 0);  dirs[1] = int2(-px0, 0);
        dirs[2] = int2(0, pz0);  dirs[3] = int2(0, -pz0);
    }
}

// =========================================================================
// CSClear -- FluidReferenceCPU.ClearPass
// §7.3: "reset claim cells for active regions to a NONE sentinel."
// Dispatched over the region rather than over a touched-list: on the GPU the
// whole-region reset is one coherent write per cell and needs no bookkeeping,
// which is the cheaper AND simpler shape here even though the CPU reference
// keeps a touched-list.
// =========================================================================
[numthreads(64, 1, 1)]
void CSClear(uint3 id : SV_DispatchThreadID)
{
    uint i = id.x;
    if (i >= _RegionCellCount) return;
    ClaimBuffer[i] = NONE;
    ReactedBuffer[i] = 0;
    WakeMark[i] = 0;
}

// =========================================================================
// CSPromote -- FluidReferenceCPU.TryPromote, driven by the CPU's wake scan.
// §7.6: "Any adjacent edit re-promotes: the edit path scans the edit's
// neighbourhood for fluid/falling materials and wakes GPU slots -- this wake
// signal is a small CPU->GPU upload, not a readback, so it is immediate."
// =========================================================================
uint AllocSlot()
{
    // NOT the claim path. See the header note on 8.4.
    uint idx;
    InterlockedAdd(Counters[1], 1u, idx);
    return idx;
}

[numthreads(64, 1, 1)]
void CSPromote(uint3 id : SV_DispatchThreadID)
{
    // DIAGNOSTIC, thread 0 only, BEFORE any early-out: proves whether this
    // kernel executed at all and what scalar uniforms it actually saw. A zero
    // in promote.seen has two causes -- the kernel never ran, or it ran with
    // _WakeRequestCount==0 -- and they are indistinguishable without this.
    if (id.x == 0)
    {
        DebugCounters[12] = 0xABCDu;              // "CSPromote executed"
        DebugCounters[13] = _WakeRequestCount;
        DebugCounters[14] = _RegionCellCount;
        DebugCounters[15] = (uint)_Tick;
        DebugCounters[17] = SampleVoxel(RegionVoxel(WakeRequests[0]));  // what terrain the GPU actually reads
    }

    uint i = id.x;
    if (i >= _WakeRequestCount) return;

    DBG(0);
    int cell = WakeRequests[i];
    if (cell < 0 || (uint)cell >= _RegionCellCount) return;
    if (SlotAtBuffer[cell] != NONE) { DBG(2); return; }   // already has a slot

    int3 v = RegionVoxel(cell);
    uint m = SampleVoxel(v);
    if (!IsMobile(m)) { DBG(3); return; }
    if (!WithinActiveRadius(v)) { DBG(16); return; }   // distinct from not-mobile

    uint s = AllocSlot();
    if (s >= _SlotCapacity)
    {
        // §7.7: "Underflow on promotion is a guarded no-op -- retry next tick.
        // No invalid write, ever." The byte stays in terrain, so nothing is lost.
        return;
    }

    // EVERY FIELD ASSIGNED, AND SetHome DELIBERATELY NOT USED HERE.
    // This previously built the slot by assigning two fields and then calling
    // SetHome(inout FluidSlot, ...), which reads the whole struct through the
    // inout. Metal's compiler rejects that outright:
    //   "'SetHome': output parameter 's' not completely initialized at kernel
    //    CSPromote (on metal)"
    // Unity then dropped kernel index 1 and SILENTLY SKIPPED every CSPromote
    // dispatch -- no slots were ever allocated, so Intent and Commit had
    // nothing to do and the whole CA looked like it was running and doing
    // nothing. Inlining the home computation removes the inout entirely.
    FluidSlot slot;
    slot.brickDataIndex   = cell >> 9;
    slot.localVoxelOffset = (uint)(cell & 511);
    slot.materialID       = m;
    slot.sleepCounter     = 0;
    slot.viscosityPhase   = 0;
    slot.stateFlags       = FLAG_AWAKE;
    FluidSlots[s] = slot;
    SlotAtBuffer[cell] = (int)s;
    DBG(1);

    // Grow the high-water mark so CSIntent/CSSweep know how far to scan.
    uint prev;
    InterlockedMax(Counters[0], s + 1, prev);
}

/// Face neighbours for the reaction scan (§7.6 scans face-adjacent cells).
int3 FaceOffset(int f)
{
    if (f == 0) return int3( 1, 0, 0);
    if (f == 1) return int3(-1, 0, 0);
    if (f == 2) return int3( 0, 1, 0);
    if (f == 3) return int3( 0,-1, 0);
    if (f == 4) return int3( 0, 0, 1);
    return int3(0, 0, -1);
}

// =========================================================================
// CSReact -- FluidReferenceCPU.TryReact, lifted into its OWN PASS.
//
// THE ONE STRUCTURAL DEVIATION FROM THE CPU REFERENCE, AND WHY. On the CPU,
// reactions run inside the Intent loop and reserve their cells before any later
// slot evaluates, because the loop is sequential. On the GPU, Intent threads run
// concurrently, so a reaction reserving a cell and another thread claiming that
// same cell would race with no ordering to resolve it -- and unlike the claim
// race (§7.3), THAT race is not safe: a move and a reaction both landing on one
// cell breaks conservation, which is the one thing §7.3's Air-Only rule exists
// to guarantee.
//
// Splitting reactions into a separate dispatch puts a barrier between "cells are
// reserved" and "cells are claimed", so Intent reads a fully-settled
// ReactedBuffer. This changes WHEN a reaction resolves relative to a move by at
// most one pass; §7.8 permits that (steady-state invariants, never frame-exact
// positions) and conservation is preserved exactly.
// =========================================================================
[numthreads(64, 1, 1)]
void CSReact(uint3 id : SV_DispatchThreadID)
{
    uint s = id.x;
    if (s >= Counters[0] || s >= _SlotCapacity) return;

    FluidSlot slot = FluidSlots[s];
    if ((slot.stateFlags & FLAG_AWAKE) == 0u) return;

    int home = HomeIndexOf(slot);
    if (home < 0 || (uint)home >= _RegionCellCount) return;
    int3 c = RegionVoxel(home);
    if (SampleVoxel(c) != slot.materialID) return;   // orphan; CSIntent frees it

    [unroll]
    for (int f = 0; f < 6; f++)
    {
        int3 n = c + FaceOffset(f);
        if (!InRegion(n)) continue;
        uint other = SampleVoxel(n);
        uint selfProduct = ReactionSelfProduct[slot.materialID * 256u + other];
        if (selfProduct == 0xFFFFFFFFu) continue;
        uint otherProduct = ReactionOtherProduct[slot.materialID * 256u + other];

        // Plain writes. If the counterpart slot reacts too it writes the same
        // products to the same two cells -- an identical-value race, harmless.
        ReactedBuffer[home] = 1;
        ReactedBuffer[RegionIndex(n)] = 1;

        // Single-cell: each side expects its own current material to still be
        // there, so an edit that changed it drops the op instead of stomping it.
        EmitOp(c, selfProduct, int3(0,0,0), 0u, slot.materialID);
        EmitOp(n, otherProduct, int3(0,0,0), 0u, other);

        // This slot is gone. Its counterpart self-frees on its next Intent via
        // the orphan check once the CPU applies the op (§7.3's mechanism).
        slot.stateFlags = 0;
        FluidSlots[s] = slot;
        if (SlotAtBuffer[home] == (int)s) SlotAtBuffer[home] = NONE;
        return;
    }
}

// =========================================================================
// CSIntent -- FluidReferenceCPU.IntentPass, including the plain-write claim.
// =========================================================================
bool TryClaim(uint s, inout FluidSlot slot, int3 dst)
{
    if (!InRegion(dst)) return false;
    int d = RegionIndex(dst);

    // THE conservation rule (§7.3): "a legal destination must have been Air at
    // tick-start." Nothing in Clear, React or Intent writes terrain, so the
    // clipmap still holds tick-start state here -- which is exactly why
    // reactions defer their writes to the op-list instead of touching terrain.
    if (SampleVoxel(dst) != AIR) return false;
    if (ReactedBuffer[d] != 0) return false;

    // §7.3, 8.4: PLAIN STORE. Not InterlockedMin. If two sources target this
    // cell both write the same aligned word; one of the two values survives and
    // neither is torn. Which one is arbitrary and that is explicitly fine.
    ClaimBuffer[d] = (int)s;
    slot.stateFlags |= FLAG_BID_PLACED;
    DBG(5);
    return true;
}

[numthreads(64, 1, 1)]
void CSIntent(uint3 id : SV_DispatchThreadID)
{
    uint s = id.x;
    if (s >= Counters[0] || s >= _SlotCapacity) return;

    FluidSlot slot = FluidSlots[s];
    if ((slot.stateFlags & FLAG_AWAKE) == 0u) return;
    DBG(4);

    slot.stateFlags &= ~(FLAG_BID_PLACED | FLAG_WON_CLAIM | FLAG_EVALUATED | FLAG_DESCENDED);

    int home = HomeIndexOf(slot);
    if (home < 0 || (uint)home >= _RegionCellCount) { FluidSlots[s] = slot; return; }
    int3 c = RegionVoxel(home);

    // ---- Orphan self-free (§7.3), BEFORE any movement ----
    if (SampleVoxel(c) != slot.materialID)
    {
        DBG(8);
        slot.stateFlags = 0;
        FluidSlots[s] = slot;
        if (SlotAtBuffer[home] == (int)s) SlotAtBuffer[home] = NONE;
        return;
    }

    // Ownership guard. PHASE_5A_COMPLETION.md §6 proved this unreachable in the
    // single-threaded CPU reference and retained it as defence-in-depth for
    // exactly this port -- here the ordering freedom that makes it reachable
    // genuinely exists, so on the GPU it is doing real work, not standing by.
    if (SlotAtBuffer[home] != (int)s)
    {
        slot.stateFlags = 0;
        FluidSlots[s] = slot;
        return;
    }

    if (ReactedBuffer[home] != 0)
    {
        slot.stateFlags = 0;
        FluidSlots[s] = slot;
        if (SlotAtBuffer[home] == (int)s) SlotAtBuffer[home] = NONE;
        return;
    }

    // ---- §7.4 near-player scope / §7.7 forced demotion ----
    if (!WithinActiveRadius(c))
    {
        slot.stateFlags = FLAG_FORCE_DEMOTE;   // clears AWAKE
        FluidSlots[s] = slot;
        if (SlotAtBuffer[home] == (int)s) SlotAtBuffer[home] = NONE;
        return;
    }

    // ---- §7.4 viscosity gate (A.5's per-slot phase counter, no modulo) ----
    uint interval = TickIntervalOf(slot.materialID);
    slot.viscosityPhase++;
    if (slot.viscosityPhase < interval) { FluidSlots[s] = slot; return; }
    slot.viscosityPhase = 0;

    slot.stateFlags |= FLAG_EVALUATED;

    // ---- §7.4's Intent hierarchy, in order. First legal destination wins, and
    // ---- a slot bids EXACTLY ONCE, which is what makes Commit single-writer.
    bool bid = TryClaim(s, slot, int3(c.x, c.y - 1, c.z));

    int2 dirs[4];
    if (!bid)
    {
        LateralOrder(c, 0, dirs);
        for (int k = 0; k < 4 && !bid; k++)
            bid = TryClaim(s, slot, int3(c.x + dirs[k].x, c.y - 1, c.z + dirs[k].y));
    }
    if (!bid && IsFluidMaterial(slot.materialID))
    {
        // §7.5 limits falling solids to down + down-diagonals; that restriction
        // is what gives sand an angle of repose instead of spreading flat.
        LateralOrder(c, 1, dirs);
        for (int k = 0; k < 4 && !bid; k++)
            bid = TryClaim(s, slot, int3(c.x + dirs[k].x, c.y, c.z + dirs[k].y));
    }

    if (!bid) DBG(9);
    FluidSlots[s] = slot;
}

// =========================================================================
// CSCommit -- FluidReferenceCPU.CommitPass. §7.3: "a second pass dispatches over
// Air destination cells (not sources). Each destination reads its own claim
// slot... that destination is the ONLY thread in the entire dispatch that will
// ever write to that cell or to the winning source's vacated home cell."
// =========================================================================
[numthreads(64, 1, 1)]
void CSCommit(uint3 id : SV_DispatchThreadID)
{
    uint d = id.x;
    if (d >= _RegionCellCount) return;

    int s = ClaimBuffer[d];
    if (s == NONE) return;
    DBG(6);
    if ((uint)s >= _SlotCapacity) return;

    FluidSlot slot = FluidSlots[s];
    if ((slot.stateFlags & FLAG_AWAKE) == 0u) return;   // freed by a reaction after bidding

    int home = HomeIndexOf(slot);
    if (home < 0 || (uint)home >= _RegionCellCount) return;
    int3 hv = RegionVoxel(home);
    int3 dv = RegionVoxel((int)d);

    if (SampleVoxel(hv) != slot.materialID) { DBG(10); return; }  // orphaned between Intent and Commit
    if (SlotAtBuffer[home] != s) { DBG(10); return; }
    if (SampleVoxel(dv) != AIR) { DBG(11); return; }              // must still be the Air it claimed
    if (ReactedBuffer[d] != 0 || ReactedBuffer[home] != 0) return;

    bool descended = dv.y < hv.y;

    // The two ops that ARE the move. Terrain is not touched here; the CPU
    // applies both through ChunkStore.SetVoxel (§7.2, §0.1 invariant 1).
    // ONLY A DESCENDING MOVE WAKES -- ported as BEHAVIOUR from 5a (see header).
    // A lateral shuffle changes no fluid level, and waking from it re-promotes
    // sleeping neighbours with a fresh budget, sustaining the shuffle forever.
    // ONE record for the whole move: dst must still be Air and src must still
    // hold the material, or the CPU applies neither half.
    uint wake = descended ? OP_WAKE_BIT : 0u;
    EmitOp(dv, slot.materialID | wake, hv, OP_HAS_SRC, AIR);
    DBG(7);

    // ONLY A DESCENDING MOVE WAKES (5a's reading, ported as behaviour): a
    // lateral shuffle changes no fluid level, and waking from it re-promotes
    // sleeping neighbours with a fresh budget and sustains the shuffle forever.
    // WakeMark values: 1 = NARROW (only what can descend into this cell),
    //                   2 = BROAD  (the full 3x3x3 neighbourhood).
    //
    // Vacating a cell ALWAYS creates a downward opportunity for whatever sits
    // above it, lateral move or not. Marking only on descend left a drop that
    // had already slept above a laterally-departing neighbour stranded with Air
    // beneath it forever -- reproduced in the oracle on a staircase floor
    // (FluidSlopedTerrainTests) and fixed there first. The narrow mark cannot
    // reintroduce the never-resting shuffle, because it never wakes a lateral
    // neighbour at the same level.
    WakeMark[home] = 1;
    if (descended)
    {
        WakeMark[home] = 2;
        WakeMark[d] = 2;
    }

    SlotAtBuffer[home] = NONE;
    SlotAtBuffer[d]    = s;
    SetHome(slot, (int)d);
    slot.stateFlags |= FLAG_WON_CLAIM;
    if (descended) slot.stateFlags |= FLAG_DESCENDED;
    FluidSlots[s] = slot;

}

// =========================================================================
// CSSweep -- FluidReferenceCPU.PostCommitSweep. §7.6 sleep, with 5a's reading:
// the counter resets only on a move that made progress DOWNWARD.
// =========================================================================
[numthreads(64, 1, 1)]
void CSSweep(uint3 id : SV_DispatchThreadID)
{
    uint s = id.x;
    if (s >= Counters[0] || s >= _SlotCapacity) return;

    FluidSlot slot = FluidSlots[s];
    if ((slot.stateFlags & FLAG_AWAKE) == 0u) return;

    // Viscosity-gated this tick: it never got a turn, so it must not age --
    // without this, honey (interval 30) would be freed by the sleep threshold
    // before ever taking a turn and would be immobile rather than slow.
    if ((slot.stateFlags & FLAG_EVALUATED) == 0u) return;

    if ((slot.stateFlags & (FLAG_WON_CLAIM | FLAG_DESCENDED)) == (FLAG_WON_CLAIM | FLAG_DESCENDED))
    {
        slot.sleepCounter = 0;
        FluidSlots[s] = slot;
        return;
    }

    if (slot.sleepCounter < 255u) slot.sleepCounter++;
    if (slot.sleepCounter >= _SleepTicks)
    {
        // §7.6: "nothing to write back, the byte already holds the material."
        // Freeing a slot costs simulation, never mass.
        int home = HomeIndexOf(slot);
        slot.stateFlags = 0;
        FluidSlots[s] = slot;
        if (home >= 0 && (uint)home < _RegionCellCount && SlotAtBuffer[home] == (int)s)
            SlotAtBuffer[home] = NONE;
        return;
    }
    FluidSlots[s] = slot;
}

// =========================================================================
// CSFinalize -- publishes the op count into the op buffer's header element so
// the CPU needs exactly ONE readback, of one buffer, per frame. Single thread.
// =========================================================================
[numthreads(1, 1, 1)]
void CSFinalize(uint3 id : SV_DispatchThreadID)
{
    if (id.x != 0) return;
    uint n = OpCounters[0];
    FluidWriteOp header;
    header.dst = int3(min(n, _MaxOpsPerFrame), 0, 0);   // .x = op count, clamped
    header.material = 0xFEEDu;                           // recognisable in a dump
    header.src = int3(0, 0, 0);
    header.flags = 0u;
    OpsBuffer[0] = header;
}

// =========================================================================
// CSWakeScan -- immediate, GPU-side re-promotion around this tick's descending
// commits. FluidReferenceCPU.WakeNeighbourhood, run where it can be instant.
// Dispatched over the region AFTER CSCommit, so WakeMark is fully settled.
// =========================================================================
[numthreads(64, 1, 1)]
void CSWakeScan(uint3 id : SV_DispatchThreadID)
{
    uint i = id.x;
    if (i >= _RegionCellCount) return;
    if (SlotAtBuffer[i] != NONE) return;              // already owned

    int3 c = RegionVoxel((int)i);
    uint m = SampleVoxel(c);
    if (!IsMobile(m)) return;
    if (!WithinActiveRadius(c)) return;

    bool near = false;

    // NARROW (mark 1 or 2): can THIS cell descend into a vacated one? Exactly
    // the five cells §7.4's tiers 1 and 2 let it reach -- straight down plus
    // the four down-diagonals. Nothing at the same level qualifies.
    int3 below[5] = {
        int3(0, -1, 0), int3(-1, -1, 0), int3(1, -1, 0), int3(0, -1, -1), int3(0, -1, 1)
    };
    [unroll]
    for (int b = 0; b < 5; b++)
    {
        int3 n = c + below[b];
        if (!InRegion(n)) continue;
        if (WakeMark[RegionIndex(n)] != 0) near = true;
    }

    // BROAD (mark 2 only): a descending move genuinely changed the local level,
    // so the whole 3x3x3 gets to re-evaluate.
    [loop] for (int dz = -1; dz <= 1 && !near; dz++)
    [loop] for (int dy = -1; dy <= 1 && !near; dy++)
    [loop] for (int dx = -1; dx <= 1 && !near; dx++)
    {
        int3 n = c + int3(dx, dy, dz);
        if (!InRegion(n)) continue;
        if (WakeMark[RegionIndex(n)] == 2) near = true;
    }
    if (!near) return;

    uint s = AllocSlot();
    if (s >= _SlotCapacity) return;                   // §7.7 guarded no-op

    FluidSlot slot;
    slot.brickDataIndex   = (int)i >> 9;
    slot.localVoxelOffset = (uint)((int)i & 511);
    slot.materialID       = m;
    slot.sleepCounter     = 0;
    slot.viscosityPhase   = 0;
    slot.stateFlags       = FLAG_AWAKE;
    FluidSlots[s] = slot;
    SlotAtBuffer[i] = (int)s;
    uint prev; InterlockedMax(Counters[0], s + 1, prev);
    DBG(1);
}


// ==========================================
// FILE: Assets/CoreEngine/Simulation/FluidClaimStress.compute
// ==========================================
// Assets/CoreEngine/Simulation/FluidClaimStress.compute
//
// §7.3's mandated Metal verification, isolated to the smallest thing that can
// answer the question:
//
//   "Still verify on Metal specifically in Phase 5b -- a stated hardware
//    guarantee is not the same as a measurement on this actual toolchain, and
//    that verification is cheap (write a stress test that floods one
//    destination cell with hundreds of contending sources, assert the surviving
//    value is always one of the valid candidates, never garbage)."
//
// It deliberately touches NO terrain, no clipmap, no slots. It is the claim
// write and nothing else, so a failure here cannot be confused with a bug in
// the CA.
//
// THE CLAIM IS A PLAIN STORE. No InterlockedMin, no atomics (§7.3, 8.4). That
// is the thing under test -- "tidying" this into an atomic would make the test
// pass by removing the question.

#pragma kernel CSSeed
#pragma kernel CSFlood

RWStructuredBuffer<int>  Claims;      // one entry per contested destination cell
RWStructuredBuffer<uint> Verdict;     // [0]=garbageCount [1]=untouchedCount [2]=distinctWinners

uint _DestCount;        // contested cells
uint _SourcesPerDest;   // contending writers per cell (hundreds, per §7.3)
uint _Pass;             // varies the candidate range between passes

#define NONE (-1)

[numthreads(64,1,1)]
void CSSeed(uint3 id : SV_DispatchThreadID)
{
    if (id.x >= _DestCount) return;
    Claims[id.x] = NONE;
}

// Every thread is a "source" writing its own id into the destination's claim
// slot with an ORDINARY STORE. Candidate ids for destination d are exactly
// [d*_SourcesPerDest, (d+1)*_SourcesPerDest), so the CPU can check the survivor
// is one of them without needing to know which thread physically landed last.
[numthreads(64,1,1)]
void CSFlood(uint3 id : SV_DispatchThreadID)
{
    uint t = id.x;
    if (t >= _DestCount * _SourcesPerDest) return;

    uint dest = t / _SourcesPerDest;
    uint candidate = t;            // globally unique, and decodable back to dest

    // *** THE LINE UNDER TEST *** plain aligned 32-bit store, contended by
    // _SourcesPerDest threads. §7.3 asserts this cannot tear.
    Claims[dest] = (int)candidate;
}


// ==========================================
// FILE: Assets/CoreEngine/Simulation/FluidGpuSimulation.cs
// ==========================================
// ==========================================
// Assets/CoreEngine/Simulation/FluidGpuSimulation.cs
//
// Phase 5b: buffer ownership and per-tick dispatch for FluidCA.compute.
//
// §13 lists two files for this phase (FluidCA.compute, FluidOpListReadback.cs);
// this is the seam between them. It owns the GPU-resident fluid state (§3.5's
// slot pool, the claim plane, the wake list, the op-list) and issues the
// Clear -> Promote -> React -> Intent+Claim -> Commit -> Sweep sequence.
// FluidOpListReadback owns the GPU->CPU half.
//
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// WHAT THIS CLASS IS NOT ALLOWED TO DO
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// It never writes terrain, on either side. The GPU decides where fluid moves;
// the decision reaches terrain only as an op-list the CPU applies through
// ChunkStore.SetVoxel (§7.2, §0.1 invariant 1). If you find yourself wanting to
// SetData terrain from here, the design has been misread.
//
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// PROMOTION IS CPU-DRIVEN, MOTION IS GPU-DRIVEN
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// §7.6: "the edit path scans the edit's neighbourhood for fluid/falling
// materials and wakes GPU slots -- this wake signal is a small CPU->GPU upload
// (§3.9), not a readback, so it is immediate." Wake requests are therefore
// uploaded, never read back. The only GPU->CPU traffic is the bounded op-list
// and the bounded descending-move wake list, both of which are appends sized to
// CHANGED cells rather than to active-slot count (§13's named failure signature
// if that is ever untrue -- FluidOpListReadback instruments it).

using System;
using System.Runtime.InteropServices;
using Unity.Mathematics;
using UnityEngine;
using UnityEngine.Rendering;
using VoxelEngine.Mirror;

namespace VoxelEngine.Simulation
{
    /// A.5 FluidSlot, CPU mirror of the HLSL struct in FluidCA.compute.
    /// MUST stay byte-identical to that struct. 24 bytes.
    [StructLayout(LayoutKind.Sequential)]
    public struct FluidSlotGpu
    {
        public int brickDataIndex;
        public uint localVoxelOffset;
        public uint materialID;
        public uint sleepCounter;
        public uint viscosityPhase;
        public uint stateFlags;
        public const int SizeBytes = 24;
    }

    /// A.9 FluidWriteOp. MUST stay byte-identical to the HLSL struct. 16 bytes.
    /// A.9 FluidWriteOp, extended to a MOVE op. MUST stay byte-identical to the
    /// HLSL struct in FluidCA.compute. 32 bytes. See that file for why a move is
    /// one record naming both cells rather than two single-cell writes.
    [StructLayout(LayoutKind.Sequential)]
    public struct FluidWriteOp
    {
        public int dx, dy, dz;
        public uint material;      // [7:0] new, [8] wake, [23:16] expected at dst
        public int sx, sy, sz;
        public uint flags;         // [0] HAS_SRC

        public const int SizeBytes = 32;
        public const uint HAS_SRC = 1u << 0;
        public const uint WAKE = 1u << 8;

        public int3 Dst => new int3(dx, dy, dz);
        public int3 Src => new int3(sx, sy, sz);
        public byte NewMaterial => (byte)(material & 0xFFu);
        public byte ExpectedAtDst => (byte)((material >> 16) & 0xFFu);
        public bool HasSrc => (flags & HAS_SRC) != 0u;
        public bool Wake => (material & WAKE) != 0u;
    }

    public sealed class FluidGpuSimulation : IDisposable
    {
        // Kernel indices, resolved once in the constructor.
        private readonly int _kClear, _kPromote, _kReact, _kIntent, _kCommit, _kSweep, _kFinalize, _kWakeScan;
        private readonly ComputeShader _cs;

        private readonly int3 _regionDims;
        private readonly int _regionCellCount;
        private readonly int _shiftX, _shiftY;
        private readonly int _slotCapacity;

        private GraphicsBuffer _slots;
        private GraphicsBuffer _claim;
        private GraphicsBuffer _slotAt;
        private GraphicsBuffer _reacted;
        private GraphicsBuffer _wakeMark;
        private GraphicsBuffer _counters;
        /// THE OP-LIST AND WAKE-OUT ARE RING-BUFFERED, AND THEY HAVE TO BE.
        /// They are written by the GPU every tick and read back ASYNCHRONOUSLY
        /// over the following 1-3 frames (§7.2). A single buffer means each
        /// tick's SetCounterValue + appends overwrite data a pending readback is
        /// still reading -- which showed up as intermittent hasError on the
        /// count readback with no logged reason, and as ops going missing.
        /// RING must exceed FluidOpListReadback.MaxFramesInFlight so a slot is
        /// never rewritten while its own readback is outstanding.
        public const int RING = 4;
        /// Element 0 is a HEADER (.voxel.x = op count); elements 1.. are the ops.
        /// One buffer, one readback request per frame -- see the note on
        /// OpsBuffer in FluidCA.compute for why the shape changed.
        private readonly GraphicsBuffer[] _ops = new GraphicsBuffer[RING];
        private readonly GraphicsBuffer[] _opCounters = new GraphicsBuffer[RING];
        private readonly uint[] _opCountersZero = new uint[4];
        private int _ring = -1;
        private GraphicsBuffer _wakeRequests;
        private GraphicsBuffer _debugCounters;
        private readonly uint[] _debugZero = new uint[DebugSlots];
        private readonly uint[] _debugScratch = new uint[DebugSlots];

        /// §10.4's per-subsystem diagnostic dump. See FluidCA.compute for the
        /// slot meanings; they are duplicated in DebugCounterNames so a dump is
        /// readable without opening the shader.
        public const int DebugSlots = 18;
        public static readonly string[] DebugCounterNames =
        {
            "promote.seen", "promote.ALLOCATED", "promote.rej_owned", "promote.rej_notmobile",
            "intent.awake", "intent.CLAIMS", "commit.claims_seen", "commit.APPLIED",
            "intent.orphan_freed", "intent.no_destination", "commit.rej_home", "commit.rej_dst_not_air",
            "PROBE.promote_ran(ABCD)", "PROBE.saw_wakecount", "PROBE.saw_regioncells", "PROBE.saw_tick",
            "promote.rej_radius", "PROBE.saw_material_at_wake0",
        };
        public GraphicsBuffer DebugCountersBuffer => _debugCounters;

        // ---------------------------------------------------------------
        // GPU CAPTURE LABELLING
        // ---------------------------------------------------------------
        // The CA used to call ComputeShader.Dispatch directly. That works, but
        // an immediate dispatch cannot carry a Metal debug group, so a captured
        // trace showed eight anonymous compute encoders per tick with no way to
        // tell CSIntent from CSCommit -- which is exactly the per-kernel
        // attribution OPTIMIZATION_CANDIDATES.md says is missing and needed to
        // rank #1 against #3.
        //
        // Recording into a CommandBuffer lets BeginSample/EndSample wrap each
        // dispatch, and Unity emits those as Metal debug groups, so Instruments
        // shows named encoders. ONE command buffer per tick, executed once, in
        // the same place the immediate dispatches were issued -- so submission
        // order relative to the readback request is unchanged.
        //
        // Parameter binding is deliberately left on the ComputeShader object
        // (BindGlobals, immediate). ComputeShader parameter state is applied at
        // dispatch time, and nothing mutates it between recording and the
        // Execute at the end of Tick.
        private CommandBuffer _cb;

        /// CAPTURE ONLY. Off in every shipping path, and the Phase 5c rig runs
        /// with it off.
        ///
        /// Metal merges consecutive compute dispatches into ONE compute encoder,
        /// and Instruments names that encoder after the FIRST debug group inside
        /// it. Measured: with all eight dispatches in one command buffer, a
        /// capture showed 710 encoder intervals all labelled
        /// "VE.FluidCA.CSClear" and none for CSPromote/CSReact/CSIntent/
        /// CSCommit/CSSweep -- one encoder covering the whole tick, named after
        /// the first sample in it.
        ///
        /// Setting this executes a command buffer PER DISPATCH, which forces an
        /// encoder boundary between kernels so each is attributed separately.
        ///
        /// IT PERTURBS WHAT IT MEASURES: eight command-buffer submissions per
        /// tick instead of one adds real per-submission cost. Use the per-kernel
        /// numbers as a RATIO between kernels, never as an absolute budget.
        public static bool SplitDispatchEncodersForCapture;

        /// Kernel labels. MUST match the names parsed by tools/parse-gpu-trace.py.
        private const string LblClear    = "VE.FluidCA.CSClear";
        private const string LblPromote  = "VE.FluidCA.CSPromote";
        private const string LblReact    = "VE.FluidCA.CSReact";
        private const string LblIntent   = "VE.FluidCA.CSIntent";
        private const string LblCommit   = "VE.FluidCA.CSCommit";
        private const string LblWakeScan = "VE.FluidCA.CSWakeScan";
        private const string LblSweep    = "VE.FluidCA.CSSweep";
        private const string LblFinalize = "VE.FluidCA.CSFinalize";

        private readonly uint[] _counterScratch = new uint[4];

        /// §10.4 diagnostic. BLOCKING read -- diagnostics and rigs only, never a
        /// timing path.
        ///   highWater     = Counters[0], the highest slot index ever bound, which
        ///                   is how far CSIntent/CSSweep scan.
        ///   everAllocated = Counters[1], the AllocSlot bump counter: the number
        ///                   of slots EVER handed out. It never decreases, because
        ///                   AllocSlot is a bump allocator with no free list, so
        ///                   comparing it against SlotCapacity is how you tell
        ///                   whether promotion has run out of indices.
        /// §10.4 diagnostic. BLOCKING, whole-buffer read -- rigs only.
        /// Returns the slot index owning this region cell, or -1 (NONE).
        ///
        /// This distinguishes the two causes of a permanently stranded voxel,
        /// which need opposite fixes: a cell with NO owner was never promoted
        /// (a wake problem), while a cell WITH an owner cannot be promoted at
        /// all -- both CSPromote and CSWakeScan return early on an owned cell --
        /// so if its slot is not awake, nothing can ever move it again.
        public int ReadSlotAtCell(int regionCell)
        {
            if (regionCell < 0 || regionCell >= _regionCellCount) return -2;
            var all = new int[_regionCellCount];
            _slotAt.GetData(all);
            return all[regionCell];
        }

        public void ReadSlotCounters(out uint highWater, out uint everAllocated)
        {
            _counters.GetData(_counterScratch);
            highWater = _counterScratch[0];
            everAllocated = _counterScratch[1];
        }

        private GraphicsBuffer _materialFlags;
        private GraphicsBuffer _materialTick;
        private GraphicsBuffer _reactSelf;
        private GraphicsBuffer _reactOther;

        private readonly int[] _wakeScratch;
        private int _wakeCount;

        /// Requests wait HERE until the GPU mirror can see the edit that caused
        /// them. See FluidWakeQueue for the frozen-fluid bug this fixes.
        private readonly FluidWakeQueue _wakePending;
        private readonly Func<int, long, bool> _mirrorReady;  // cached: called per pending request per tick
        private TerrainClipmap _mirrorForReadyTest;

        // CPU-side half of the §10.4 dump. promote.seen==0 on the GPU has two
        // completely different causes -- the CPU never queued anything, or it
        // queued and the dispatch/upload lost it -- and they are indistinguishable
        // from GPU counters alone.
        public int PendingWakeRequests => _wakeCount;
        public int LastDispatchedWakeCount { get; private set; }
        /// Cumulative, because the per-tick value is 0 on every tick after the
        /// first and a late sample therefore proves nothing about the first.
        public long WakeDispatchedTotal { get; private set; }
        public long PromoteDispatchesTotal { get; private set; }
        public long WakeRequestsQueuedTotal { get; private set; }
        public long WakeRejectedOutOfRegion { get; private set; }
        public long WakeRejectedFull { get; private set; }
        /// Requests queued but not yet dispatched because the mirror is still
        /// stale for their chunk. Steady non-zero here means uploads are behind.
        public int DeferredWakeRequests => _wakePending.PendingCount;
        public long WakeCoalescedTotal => _wakePending.CoalescedTotal;
        /// Released without the mirror ever going clean (§FluidWakeQueue.Collect).
        /// Should be 0 in a healthy run.
        public long WakeReleasedStaleTotal => _wakePending.ReleasedStaleTotal;

        public int3 RegionOriginVoxels { get; set; }
        public int3 PlayerVoxel { get; set; }
        public int ActiveRadiusVoxels { get; set; } = EngineConfig.FLUID_ACTIVE_RADIUS_VOXELS;
        public int TickCount { get; private set; }

        public int3 RegionDims => _regionDims;
        public int RegionCellCount => _regionCellCount;
        public int SlotCapacity => _slotCapacity;
        public int MaxOpsPerFrame { get; }

        /// The ring slot the most recent Tick wrote. IssueReadback must read
        /// THIS slot, not a fixed one.
        public int CurrentRing => _ring;
        /// THE only buffer the CPU reads back.
        public GraphicsBuffer OpsBuffer => _ops[_ring < 0 ? 0 : _ring];

        /// <param name="regionDims">Active-region size in voxels. EVERY component
        /// must be a power of two: FluidCA.compute addresses the region with
        /// shifts and masks (§0.1 invariant 2), and a non-power-of-two does not
        /// fail loudly, it aliases silently -- the §6.2 phantom-terrain bug
        /// class. Asserted, not trusted.</param>
        public FluidGpuSimulation(ComputeShader fluidCA, int3 regionDims,
                                  int slotCapacity, int maxOpsPerFrame)
        {
            _cs = fluidCA != null ? fluidCA
                : throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(fluidCA), "FluidCA.compute not assigned");

            RequirePow2(regionDims.x, "regionDims.x");
            RequirePow2(regionDims.y, "regionDims.y");
            RequirePow2(regionDims.z, "regionDims.z");

            _regionDims = regionDims;
            _regionCellCount = regionDims.x * regionDims.y * regionDims.z;
            _shiftX = Log2(regionDims.x);
            _shiftY = Log2(regionDims.y);
            _slotCapacity = Math.Min(slotCapacity, EngineConfig.MAX_ACTIVE_FLUID);
            MaxOpsPerFrame = maxOpsPerFrame;

            _kClear   = _cs.FindKernel("CSClear");
            _kPromote = _cs.FindKernel("CSPromote");
            _kReact   = _cs.FindKernel("CSReact");
            _kIntent  = _cs.FindKernel("CSIntent");
            _kCommit  = _cs.FindKernel("CSCommit");
            _kSweep   = _cs.FindKernel("CSSweep");
            _kFinalize = _cs.FindKernel("CSFinalize");
            _kWakeScan = _cs.FindKernel("CSWakeScan");

            _slots   = New(GraphicsBuffer.Target.Structured, _slotCapacity, FluidSlotGpu.SizeBytes);
            _claim   = New(GraphicsBuffer.Target.Structured, _regionCellCount, 4);
            _slotAt  = New(GraphicsBuffer.Target.Structured, _regionCellCount, 4);
            _reacted = New(GraphicsBuffer.Target.Structured, _regionCellCount, 4);
            _wakeMark = New(GraphicsBuffer.Target.Structured, _regionCellCount, 4);
            _counters = New(GraphicsBuffer.Target.Structured, 4, 4);
            for (int i = 0; i < RING; i++)
            {
                _ops[i] = New(GraphicsBuffer.Target.Structured, maxOpsPerFrame + 1, FluidWriteOp.SizeBytes);
                _opCounters[i] = New(GraphicsBuffer.Target.Structured, 4, 4);
            }
            _wakeRequests = New(GraphicsBuffer.Target.Structured, maxOpsPerFrame, 4);
            _cb = new CommandBuffer { name = "VE.FluidCA" };
            _wakeScratch = new int[maxOpsPerFrame];
            // MaxWakeDeferTicks: how long a request may wait for its chunk to
            // upload before being released anyway. 120 ticks is far longer than
            // any observed upload lag (a single edited chunk normally clears on
            // the very next LateUpdate) while still bounding the queue.
            _wakePending = new FluidWakeQueue(maxOpsPerFrame, MaxWakeDeferTicks);
            _mirrorReady = IsMirrorReadyForCell;
            _debugCounters = New(GraphicsBuffer.Target.Structured, DebugSlots, 4);

            // §3.7's lesson, applied here too: a fresh GraphicsBuffer contains
            // whatever was in GPU memory. SlotAt in particular MUST start at
            // NONE or CSPromote will believe every cell already owns a slot and
            // silently promote nothing.
            var noneFill = new int[_regionCellCount];
            for (int i = 0; i < _regionCellCount; i++) noneFill[i] = -1;
            _slotAt.SetData(noneFill);
            _claim.SetData(noneFill);
            _reacted.SetData(new int[_regionCellCount]);
            _wakeMark.SetData(new int[_regionCellCount]);
            _counters.SetData(new uint[4]);
            _slots.SetData(new FluidSlotGpu[_slotCapacity]);

            UploadMaterialRegistry();
        }

        private static GraphicsBuffer New(GraphicsBuffer.Target target, int count, int stride) =>
            new GraphicsBuffer(target, Math.Max(1, count), stride);

        /// §3.9's CPU->GPU registry upload, restricted to what the CA reads:
        /// A.7 flags, §7.4 tick intervals, and §7.6's reaction pairs flattened to
        /// a 256x256 lookup so the shader needs no loop over a pair table.
        private void UploadMaterialRegistry()
        {
            var flags = new uint[256];
            var interval = new uint[256];
            var reactSelf = new uint[256 * 256];
            var reactOther = new uint[256 * 256];
            for (int i = 0; i < reactSelf.Length; i++) reactSelf[i] = 0xFFFFFFFFu;

            for (int m = 0; m < 256; m++)
            {
                flags[m] = MaterialRules.Flags((byte)m);
                interval[m] = MaterialRules.TickInterval((byte)m);
                for (int o = 0; o < 256; o++)
                {
                    if (!MaterialRules.TryGetReaction((byte)m, (byte)o,
                            out byte sp, out byte op)) continue;
                    reactSelf[m * 256 + o] = sp;
                    reactOther[m * 256 + o] = op;
                }
            }

            _materialFlags = New(GraphicsBuffer.Target.Structured, 256, 4);
            _materialTick  = New(GraphicsBuffer.Target.Structured, 256, 4);
            _reactSelf     = New(GraphicsBuffer.Target.Structured, 256 * 256, 4);
            _reactOther    = New(GraphicsBuffer.Target.Structured, 256 * 256, 4);
            _materialFlags.SetData(flags);
            _materialTick.SetData(interval);
            _reactSelf.SetData(reactSelf);
            _reactOther.SetData(reactOther);
        }

        // =====================================================================
        // Wake requests (§7.6) -- uploaded, never read back
        // =====================================================================

        /// Ticks a wake request may wait for its chunk to reach the GPU.
        public const int MaxWakeDeferTicks = 120;

        public void ClearWakeRequests()
        {
            _wakeCount = 0;
            _wakePending.Clear();
        }

        /// True when the GPU clipmap already holds the chunk containing this
        /// region cell, i.e. CSPromote's SampleVoxel will read the CURRENT
        /// material rather than the pre-edit one. A chunk that was never dirty
        /// is ready by definition.
        /// Ready once the chunk has been uploaded at an epoch STRICTLY LATER
        /// than the edit that queued this request. Any such upload contains the
        /// edit, because UploadDirty copies the chunk's current CPU state.
        ///
        /// This replaced a plain !IsDirty(chunk) test, which STARVED: a cell
        /// edited every frame leaves its chunk dirty at every tick even though
        /// it is uploaded between them, so the request never came ready and
        /// only escaped via the stale timeout. The Phase 5c hold_paint case
        /// (holding the place button) measured that directly -- 8 voxels placed
        /// where 30 were asked for, 900/120 = the stale interval exactly.
        private bool IsMirrorReadyForCell(int cell, long stamp)
        {
            TerrainClipmap m = Mirror;
            if (m == null) return true;      // no mirror at all: nothing to wait for

            int3 chunk = CoordMath.VoxelToChunk(RegionVoxel(cell));

            // NOT DIRTY => the mirror already holds this chunk's current state,
            // so there is nothing to wait for and the request is ready NOW.
            //
            // This half is load-bearing and was missing at first. §8.3 wakes the
            // edited cell's whole 26-NEIGHBOURHOOD, and those neighbours are
            // routinely in a DIFFERENT chunk that was never edited and so is
            // never dirty. With only the epoch test below, no upload ever
            // advanced their chunk's epoch, so those requests waited out the
            // full MaxWakeDeferTicks. The Phase 5c large_pour case showed it as
            // voxels that looked permanently stranded but were merely 120 ticks
            // from being looked at.
            if (!m.IsDirty(chunk)) return true;

            // DIRTY => an upload is outstanding. Wait for one that happened
            // after the edit, since only such an upload can contain it.
            return m.LastUploadEpoch(chunk) > stamp;
        }

        /// The clipmap to measure readiness against. Tick() supplies it, but
        /// EDITS HAPPEN BEFORE THE FIRST TICK -- a vent places its first voxel
        /// in the same frame the scene starts simulating -- so fall back to the
        /// active mirror rather than to "no mirror".
        private TerrainClipmap Mirror => _mirrorForReadyTest ?? TerrainClipmap.Active;

        /// The mirror epoch to stamp a request with: the state of the world the
        /// edit was made against.
        ///
        /// THE DEFAULT HERE MUST BE CONSERVATIVE. Returning -1 for "I don't
        /// know the epoch yet" meant "already uploaded", which released the
        /// request on the very next tick against a mirror that did not contain
        /// the edit -- reintroducing the exact freeze this class exists to
        /// prevent, for the first edit of every scene. The Phase 5c rig caught
        /// it immediately: vent_sustained placed 1 voxel instead of 40 and left
        /// it floating. long.MaxValue instead means "not ready until a real
        /// epoch says so", so an unknown mirror errs toward waiting.
        private long CurrentMirrorStamp => Mirror?.UploadEpoch ?? long.MaxValue;

        /// Queue a world voxel to be considered for promotion next dispatch.
        /// Silently drops out-of-region coordinates and overflow, both of which
        /// are "this cell does not move this tick", never a lost byte.
        public void RequestWake(int3 worldVoxel)
        {
            if (!InRegion(worldVoxel)) { WakeRejectedOutOfRegion++; return; }
            if (!_wakePending.Add(RegionIndex(worldVoxel), CurrentMirrorStamp)) { WakeRejectedFull++; return; }
            WakeRequestsQueuedTotal++;
        }

        /// §8.3's "scan 26-neighborhood for fluid/falling materials -> wake slots".
        public void RequestWakeNeighbourhood(int3 worldVoxel)
        {
            for (int dz = -1; dz <= 1; dz++)
            for (int dy = -1; dy <= 1; dy++)
            for (int dx = -1; dx <= 1; dx++)
                RequestWake(worldVoxel + new int3(dx, dy, dz));
        }

        public void RequestWakeRegionCell(int regionCell)
        {
            if (regionCell < 0 || regionCell >= _regionCellCount) { WakeRejectedOutOfRegion++; return; }
            if (!_wakePending.Add(regionCell, CurrentMirrorStamp)) { WakeRejectedFull++; return; }
            WakeRequestsQueuedTotal++;
        }

        public bool InRegion(int3 v)
        {
            int3 r = v - RegionOriginVoxels;
            return r.x >= 0 && r.y >= 0 && r.z >= 0 &&
                   r.x < _regionDims.x && r.y < _regionDims.y && r.z < _regionDims.z;
        }

        public int RegionIndex(int3 v)
        {
            int3 r = v - RegionOriginVoxels;
            return r.x | (r.y << _shiftX) | (r.z << (_shiftX + _shiftY));
        }

        public int3 RegionVoxel(int index)
        {
            int mx = _regionDims.x - 1, my = _regionDims.y - 1;
            return new int3(index & mx, (index >> _shiftX) & my,
                            index >> (_shiftX + _shiftY)) + RegionOriginVoxels;
        }

        // =====================================================================
        // The tick
        // =====================================================================

        /// One CA tick: Clear -> Promote -> React -> Intent+Claim -> Commit -> Sweep.
        /// Each stage is its own dispatch, which is what puts a barrier between
        /// them -- CSReact in particular RELIES on that barrier (see its header).
        public void Tick(TerrainClipmap clipmap)
        {
            if (clipmap == null) throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(clipmap));
            TickCount++;

            // Release only the requests the GPU can actually act on. When the
            // mirror is already current -- every rig and every existing test --
            // this releases them on the same tick they were queued, so nothing
            // about existing behaviour changes.
            _mirrorForReadyTest = clipmap;
            _wakeCount = _wakePending.Collect(_mirrorReady, _wakeScratch, _wakeScratch.Length);

            _ring = (_ring + 1) % RING;          // advance BEFORE binding
            _opCounters[_ring].SetData(_opCountersZero);
            // Cleared every tick: these are PER-TICK counters, and a running
            // total would hide which tick a stage went silent on.
            _debugCounters.SetData(_debugZero);
            LastDispatchedWakeCount = _wakeCount;
            WakeDispatchedTotal += _wakeCount;
            if (_wakeCount > 0) _wakeRequests.SetData(_wakeScratch, 0, 0, _wakeCount);

            BindGlobals(clipmap);

            if (!SplitDispatchEncodersForCapture) _cb.Clear();
            Dispatch(_kClear, _regionCellCount, LblClear);
            if (_wakeCount > 0) { Dispatch(_kPromote, _wakeCount, LblPromote); PromoteDispatchesTotal++; }
            Dispatch(_kReact, _slotCapacity, LblReact);
            Dispatch(_kIntent, _slotCapacity, LblIntent);
            Dispatch(_kCommit, _regionCellCount, LblCommit);
            Dispatch(_kWakeScan, _regionCellCount, LblWakeScan);   // immediate GPU-side wake
            Dispatch(_kSweep, _slotCapacity, LblSweep);
            Dispatch(_kFinalize, 1, LblFinalize);   // publish the count into ops[0]
            if (!SplitDispatchEncodersForCapture) Graphics.ExecuteCommandBuffer(_cb);

            _wakeCount = 0;
        }

        private void BindGlobals(TerrainClipmap clipmap)
        {
            _cs.SetInts("_RegionOriginVoxels", RegionOriginVoxels.x, RegionOriginVoxels.y, RegionOriginVoxels.z, 0);
            _cs.SetInts("_RegionDimsVoxels", _regionDims.x, _regionDims.y, _regionDims.z, 0);
            _cs.SetInts("_RegionShifts", _shiftX, _shiftY, 0, 0);
            _cs.SetInts("_PlayerVoxel", PlayerVoxel.x, PlayerVoxel.y, PlayerVoxel.z, 0);
            _cs.SetInt("_ActiveRadiusVoxels", ActiveRadiusVoxels);
            _cs.SetInt("_Tick", TickCount);
            _cs.SetInt("_SlotCapacity", _slotCapacity);
            _cs.SetInt("_RegionCellCount", _regionCellCount);
            _cs.SetInt("_WakeRequestCount", _wakeCount);
            _cs.SetInt("_MaxOpsPerFrame", MaxOpsPerFrame);
            _cs.SetInt("_SleepTicks", EngineConfig.FLUID_SLEEP_TICKS);

            int3 wdc = clipmap.WindowDimsChunks, wdb = clipmap.WindowDimsBricks, wob = clipmap.WindowOriginBricks;
            _cs.SetInts("_WindowDimsChunksPacked", wdc.x, wdc.y, wdc.z, 0);
            _cs.SetInts("_WindowDimsBricksPacked", wdb.x, wdb.y, wdb.z, 0);
            _cs.SetInts("_WindowOriginBricksPacked", wob.x, wob.y, wob.z, 0);

            foreach (int k in new[] { _kClear, _kPromote, _kReact, _kIntent, _kCommit, _kSweep, _kFinalize, _kWakeScan })
            {
                _cs.SetBuffer(k, "ClipmapBuffer", clipmap.ClipmapBuffer);
                _cs.SetBuffer(k, "BrickDataBuffer", clipmap.BrickDataBuffer);
                _cs.SetBuffer(k, "FluidSlots", _slots);
                _cs.SetBuffer(k, "ClaimBuffer", _claim);
                _cs.SetBuffer(k, "SlotAtBuffer", _slotAt);
                _cs.SetBuffer(k, "ReactedBuffer", _reacted);
                _cs.SetBuffer(k, "WakeMark", _wakeMark);
                _cs.SetBuffer(k, "Counters", _counters);
                _cs.SetBuffer(k, "OpsBuffer", _ops[_ring]);
                _cs.SetBuffer(k, "OpCounters", _opCounters[_ring]);
                _cs.SetBuffer(k, "WakeRequests", _wakeRequests);
                _cs.SetBuffer(k, "DebugCounters", _debugCounters);
                _cs.SetBuffer(k, "MaterialFlags", _materialFlags);
                _cs.SetBuffer(k, "MaterialTickInterval", _materialTick);
                _cs.SetBuffer(k, "ReactionSelfProduct", _reactSelf);
                _cs.SetBuffer(k, "ReactionOtherProduct", _reactOther);
            }
        }

        private void Dispatch(int kernel, int threads, string label)
        {
            if (threads <= 0) return;
            if (SplitDispatchEncodersForCapture)
            {
                // One command buffer per dispatch => one encoder per kernel.
                _cb.Clear();
                _cb.BeginSample(label);
                _cb.DispatchCompute(_cs, kernel, (threads + 63) / 64, 1, 1);
                _cb.EndSample(label);
                Graphics.ExecuteCommandBuffer(_cb);
                return;
            }
            _cb.BeginSample(label);
            _cb.DispatchCompute(_cs, kernel, (threads + 63) / 64, 1, 1);
            _cb.EndSample(label);
        }

        // =====================================================================

        private static void RequirePow2(int v, string name)
        {
            if (v <= 0 || (v & (v - 1)) != 0)
                throw new ArgumentException($"{name} must be a positive power of two (got {v}).", name);
        }

        private static int Log2(int p) { int n = 0; while ((p >> n) > 1) n++; return n; }

        /// Blocking read of this tick's diagnostic counters. Rig/debug only --
        /// it stalls the pipeline, which is exactly why it is not on any
        /// shipped path.
        public uint[] ReadDebugCountersBlocking()
        {
            _debugCounters.GetData(_debugScratch);
            return _debugScratch;
        }

        /// One-line §10.4 dump of the last tick's per-stage activity.
        public string DebugDump()
        {
            uint[] c = ReadDebugCountersBlocking();
